productBrief: cortex: synthetic focus-group platform with persistent AI personas

transcript.speaker: dd796e3f06d81ced2186ffb11088162961e276d69f9f32f5871248f76b3ea48c
transcript.text: My mom would get confused by the abstract responses. She needs clear, actionable advice, not vague feedback.

transcript.speaker: aecf5de578f6ddd4528aa2a69ba7c85b33f1f355737a23e11d1cce5bc1f1057d
transcript.text: The persistent AI personas feel a bit too abstract. My mom struggled with AI assistants that couldn't understand her requests, so I'm wary of another layer of complexity.

transcript.speaker: 2717be3bfceeda10681e78ffab52d63cfcec0e32944d50bdbd9d21e92bd7c254
transcript.text: Sounds like vapor. Who's going to pay for synthetic feedback when real user data is so valuable? Not for me.

transcript.speaker: 10a0c43061f6c2e22dff09ca31f1ae3bc6f7b71d4e8f7b4e7022da309e95ab9b
transcript.text: Persistent AI personas sound like theater. Where's the data showing they actually improve feedback quality? Not for me.

transcript.speaker: e383017f2283397847f2666c731d4d739af15a4187f67d60566570bd5dc1ac4e
transcript.text: Persistent AI personas sound like a double-edged sword. Will they really help with actionable feedback or just feel like abstract noise? Who churns first if no one finds them useful?

transcript.speaker: 57d4b3fd74996e675e188786a1cc6c09e28133f35c6927daef676256394b7d0f
transcript.text: The idea of persistent AI personas is interesting, but I need to know how well they mimic real human feedback.Feels too abstract without concrete data.

transcript.speaker: dd796e3f06d81ced2186ffb11088162961e276d69f9f32f5871248f76b3ea48c
transcript.text: I get what you're missing, but my mom had trouble distinguishing between AI and human feedback during testing. It felt very real to her, and that's what matters. We need concrete data, not just abstract assumptions.

transcript.speaker: aecf5de578f6ddd4528aa2a69ba7c85b33f1f355737a23e11d1cce5bc1f1057d
transcript.text: Persistent AI personas might feel abstract, but imagine my mom trying to give detailed feedback—she'd struggle. We need concrete data on how well they mimic real humans before I'm convinced.

transcript.speaker: 2717be3bfceeda10681e78ffab52d63cfcec0e32944d50bdbd9d21e92bd7c254
transcript.text: Persistent AI personas need to mimic real human feedback closely to avoid feeling abstract. But who cares if they're close if they don't actually provide better insights or actions? What's the price point for this feature?

transcript.speaker: 10a0c43061f6c2e22dff09ca31f1ae3bc6f7b71d4e8f7b4e7022da309e95ab9b
transcript.text: Persistent AI personas are overhyped. I've seen similar concepts fail before—lacks empirical evidence of mimicking real feedback effectively.

transcript.speaker: e383017f2283397847f2666c731d4d739af15a4187f67d60566570bd5dc1ac4e
transcript.text: Feels too abstract without concrete data. How about we run a pilot with a few users to see if the AI personas provide any meaningful insights before committing resources? Who needs theater when you can have real feedback?

transcript.text: Feels too abstract without concrete data. I've seen similar claims before, and they usually end up being just surface-level behavior. Where's the proof they can handle real-world scenarios?
